title: Flat at a prime with smooth fibre implies smooth at the prime
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Let $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] and $\mathfrak Q\subset F$ the kernel of the ring map $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\bar\lambda$ (the prime of $F$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$). Assume (1) there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $S_g$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; (2) the local ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ induced by $\varphi$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; (3) $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F$ is smooth at $\mathfrak Q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. Then $R\to S$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00TF (lemma-flat-fibre-smooth, line 37673) and its proof (Lemmas 00SY lemma-syntomic, 00T5 lemma-smooth-over-field, 00TE lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection-smooth); used in Smoothing 07CP (line 1580)

proof.text:
(The fibre is a global complete intersection near $\mathfrak Q$.) Write $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. By hypothesis (3) and [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal] there is $h\in F\setminus\mathfrak Q$ such that $F_h$ is a smooth $k$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-local-complete-intersection] $F_h$ is a local complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]: there are $e_i\in F_h$ ($i\in J$) with $\operatorname{Spec}F_h= igcup_iD(e_i)$ and every $(F_h)_{e_i}$ a global complete intersection over $k$. The ideal $\mathfrak QF_h$ is prime since $h
otin\mathfrak Q$, so it lies in some $D(e_i)$; write $e_i=a/h^m$ with $a\in F$; then $a
otin\mathfrak Q$ (otherwise $e_i\in\mathfrak QF_h$), hence $h'=ha
otin\mathfrak Q$. The composite $F	o F_h	o(F_h)_{e_i}$ is a localization of $F$ at $\{(ha)^N\}$ in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization]: $ha\mapsto(h/1)(a/1)=h^{m+1}e_i/1$ is a unit; every element $(x/h^l)/e_i^j=xh^{mj}/(h^la^j)$ equals $y/(ha)^{l+j}$ with $y=xh^{mj+j}a^l$ (multiply numerator and denominator by $h^ja^l$); and $x\mapsto0$ means $e_i^j(x/1)=0$ in $F_h$, i.e. $h^ua^jx=0$ in $F$ for some $u$, so $(ha)^{\max(u,j)}x=0$. Hence $(F_h)_{e_i}\cong F_{h'}$ as $k$-algebras, and $F_{h'}$ is a global complete intersection over $k$ (the definition is invariant under $k$-algebra isomorphism).

proof.text: (A relative global complete intersection near $\mathfrak q$.) Hypotheses (1), (2) of the statement and step 1 (with $h'\in F\setminus\mathfrak Q$) are the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-syntomic-at-prime-relative-global-complete-intersection]. Hence there are $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$, integers $n,c\ge0$, $f_1,\dots,f_c\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ such that $T=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $\theta:S_g\xrightarrow{\sim}T$. Since $g\notin\mathfrak q$, $\mathfrak qS_g$ is a prime of $S_g$ whose inverse image in $S$ is $\mathfrak q$; let $\mathfrak q_T=\theta(\mathfrak qS_g)$, a prime of $T$ whose inverse image in $R$ is $\mathfrak p$ (as $\theta$ is an $R$-algebra map), and $\kappa(\mathfrak q_T)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ compatibly with $S\to S_g\to T$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00TF (lemma-flat-fibre-smooth), lines 37689-37692 ('By Lemmas 00SY and 00T5 we see that there exists a g in S such that S_g is a relative global complete intersection')

proof.text: (The fibre of $T$.) Let $F_T=T\otimes_Rk$ and $\mathfrak Q_T\subset F_T$ the kernel of $F_T\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_T)$, $t\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar t\bar\lambda$. (a) With $A=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $A\otimes_Rk\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $p\otimes\lambda\mapsto\lambda\rho(p)$ with $\rho:A\to k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ the coefficient reduction [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension]; so $F_T=(A/(f_1,\dots,f_c))\otimes_Rk\cong(A/(f))\otimes_A(A\otimes_Rk)\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)$, $\bar f_j=\rho(f_j)$, by associativity of $\otimes$ and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] (with $B=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$, $I=(f_1,\dots,f_c)$); this isomorphism sends $(p\bmod(f))\otimes1$ to $\rho(p)\bmod(\bar f)$. (b) By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (with $A=M=S$, multiplicative set $\{g^N\}$, $N=k$), $S_g\otimes_Rk\cong(S\otimes_Rk)_{\bar g}=F_{\bar g}$, $\bar g=g\otimes1$; composed with $\theta\otimes1$ this gives a $k$-algebra isomorphism $\psi:F_{\bar g}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_T$, compatible with the maps to $\kappa(\mathfrak q)\cong\kappa(\mathfrak q_T)$ of step 2, so $\psi(\mathfrak QF_{\bar g})=\mathfrak Q_T$; note $\bar g\notin\mathfrak Q$ because $g$ has nonzero image in $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$.

proof.text: ($k\to F_T$ is a relative global complete intersection, smooth at $\mathfrak Q_T$.) Smoothness: with $h$ from step 1, $F_{\bar gh}$ is a localization of $F_h$ at the powers of $\bar g/1$ and of $F_{\bar g}$ at the powers of $h/1$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization] (check of (a)-(c) as in step 1), so $(F_{\bar g})_{h/1}\cong(F_h)_{\bar g/1}$, which is smooth over $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-principal-localization]; with $u=\psi(h/1)\notin\mathfrak Q_T$ (as $h\notin\mathfrak Q$), $(F_T)_u\cong(F_{\bar g})_{h/1}$ is a smooth $k$-algebra (smoothness [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] is invariant under isomorphism of $k$-algebras), so $k\to F_T$ is smooth at $\mathfrak Q_T$ [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. Complete intersection: by step 3(a) $F_T\cong k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)=:\bar T$. $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has the single point $(0)$ with $\kappa((0))=k$, and the fibre ring $\bar T\otimes_kk\cong\bar T\cong F_T$ is nonzero (it has the prime $\mathfrak Q_T$); since $F_T=T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a nonzero fibre ring of the relative global complete intersection $T$ (step 2), $\dim\operatorname{Spec}F_T=n-c$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection], and homeomorphic spectra have equal Krull dimension. So $\bar T=k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c)$ is a relative global complete intersection over $k$ [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection].

proof.text: (A maximal minor outside $\mathfrak Q_T$.) Let $\bar{\mathfrak Q}\subset\bar T$ be the image of $\mathfrak Q_T$ under $F_T\cong\bar T$. By step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-smooth-jacobian] ('only if', applied to $k\to\bar T$, $\bar f_1,\dots,\bar f_c$ and $\bar{\mathfrak Q}$) there is $I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$, $|I|=c$, with $\det(\partial\bar f_j/\partial x_i)_{j,\,i\in I}\bmod(\bar f)\notin\bar{\mathfrak Q}$. The coefficient reduction $\rho$ is a ring homomorphism with $\rho(\partial p/\partial x_i)=\partial\rho(p)/\partial x_i$ (check on monomials $r x^e$, [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]) and the determinant is a polynomial in the entries with integer coefficients, so $\rho(g_I)=\det(\partial\bar f_j/\partial x_i)_{j,\,i\in I}$ with $g_I=\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j,\,i\in I}\in R[x_1,\dots,x_n]$. By step 3(a), $(g_I\bmod(f))\otimes1\in F_T$ corresponds to $\rho(g_I)\bmod(\bar f)$; hence $(\bar g_I)\otimes1\notin\mathfrak Q_T$, $\bar g_I$ the image of $g_I$ in $T$.

proof.text: ($R\to T$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q_T$.) For $t\in T$, $t\otimes1\in\mathfrak Q_T$ iff the image $\bar t$ of $t$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q_T)$ is $0$ iff $t\in\mathfrak q_T$ (definition of $\mathfrak Q_T$ as the kernel of $F_T\to\kappa(\mathfrak q_T)$). So by step 5 $\bar g_I\notin\mathfrak q_T$, and [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-smooth-jacobian] ('if', applied to the relative global complete intersection $T=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ of step 2 and $\mathfrak q_T$) shows that $R\to T$ is smooth at $\mathfrak q_T$: there is $t\in T\setminus\mathfrak q_T$ with $T_t$ a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal].

split_report.summary: Statement checked against Stacks 00TF and kept (hypotheses (1)-(3) and conclusion agree; 'smooth at q' is Definition 00TB as recorded in def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal). Proof written in 7 steps following the Stacks proof: 00T5 (existing node lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-local-complete-intersection) turns the smooth fibre near Q into a global complete intersection F_{h'}; 00SY (3)=>(2) (new node lem-weil-pbc-syntomic-at-prime-relative-global-complete-intersection, hypothesis on the fibre phrased via 00SG (3) instead of 'S_q/pS_q complete intersection ring') gives S_g = R[x]/(f) a relative global complete intersection (new definition node for 00SP); the replacement of S by S_g, which Stacks leaves implicit, is written out (fibre of S_g = F_{g-bar}, tensor of a quotient of a polynomial ring with kappa(p), prime correspondence, transport of smoothness at a prime through S_g = T and principal localizations); 00TE (new node lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-smooth-jacobian) is applied to kappa(p) -> F_T (which is a relative global complete intersection over kappa(p) because its only fibre is F_T) and then to R -> T, with the compatibility of the Jacobian minors with coefficient reduction. Mathlib: Algebra.IsSmoothAt.of_formallySmooth_fiber (RingTheory/Smooth/Fiber.lean:193-237, @[stacks 00TF] with global flatness and the whole fibre formally smooth) is the closest Lean statement, not a one-line specialization; recorded on the item, no leaf.

reviewed.note: 7 steps following Stacks 00TF with the hidden checks written out: fibre a global complete intersection near Q (00T5 node, localization of localization); 00SY (3)=>(2) as a new unsplit node, stated with the 00SG-equivalent hypothesis 'F_h a global complete intersection for some h not in Q' (L checked 00SY and 00SG: equivalent to S_q/pS_q a complete intersection ring); fibre of T = k[x]/(f bar) with matching primes; k -> F_T a relative global complete intersection smooth at Q_T; a Jacobian minor outside Q_T via the new unsplit 00TE node, commuting derivatives with coefficient reduction; 00TE 'if' for R -> T; back to S by T_t = S_{gs}.
